children: Raymond Lifestyle’s Ebitda declines 2.6 per cent amid higher input costs, even as Branded Apparel revenue rises 20 per cent and Garmenting revenue grows 26 per cent

Raymond Lifestyle reported a 10.2 per cent year-on-year decline in net profit to Rs 68 crore in the September quarter, compared with Rs 75 crore a year earlier, as higher input costs and an unfavourable sales mix weighed on margins. Revenue from operations rose 13.2 per cent to Rs 2,075 crore from Rs 1,832 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) fell 2.6 per cent to Rs 220 crore from Rs 226 crore, while the Ebitda margin narrowed to 10.61 per cent from 12.33 per cent a year earlier.

Total income, including income beyond revenue from operations, increased 14 per cent to Rs 2,125 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 1,865 crore in the year-ago period. The company attributed the growth to premiumisation and casualwear demand, higher volumes in branded apparel and a recovery in international garmenting demand, particularly in the US, the UK and Europe.

For the first half of FY27, total income rose 10 per cent year-on-year to Rs 3,685 crore, while Ebitda increased 6 per cent to Rs 404 crore. The Ebitda margin for the six months ended September stood at 11 per cent.

Branded Apparel was among the key growth drivers, with quarterly revenue rising 20 per cent to a record Rs 559 crore from Rs 465 crore a year earlier. Casualwear brands ColorPlus and Parx led the increase. EBITDA grew to Rs 49 crore from Rs 41 crore, while the margin remained at 8.8 per cent. Gains from the closure of underperforming stores helped offset pressure from higher raw material costs and an adverse channel mix.

The Garmenting business recorded a 26 per cent increase in revenue to Rs 339 crore from Rs 269 crore. The company cited order execution following tariff rationalisation between India and the US, the India-UK free trade agreement and the addition of new global clients as growth drivers.
The segment’s Ebitda rose to Rs 25 crore from Rs 14 crore, lifting its margin to 7.4 per cent from 5.3 per cent a year earlier, an expansion of 207 basis points.

Revenue from Branded Textiles increased 7 per cent to Rs 971 crore from Rs 906 crore, supported by festive-season demand from distribution channels and the shift towards premium products. Ebitda was largely flat at Rs 188 crore against Rs 186 crore, while the margin declined to 19.3 per cent from 20.6 per cent due to higher raw material and freight costs.

High Value Cotton Shirting revenue grew 5 per cent to Rs 222 crore from Rs 212 crore. However, Ebitda fell to Rs 21 crore from Rs 25 crore, and the margin contracted to 9.5 per cent from 12 per cent. Higher raw material prices weighed on profitability, partly offset by an increase in average selling prices.

The Emerging Business portfolio, which includes Ethnix by Raymond, Raymond Home, Park Avenue Innerwear, Chairman’s Collections and Sexual Wellness, posted a 15 per cent rise in revenue to Rs 100 crore from Rs 87 crore.
Raymond Lifestyle Moves To Net Cash Position

Raymond Lifestyle had 1,634 stores at the end of September 2026, compared with 1,663 stores a year earlier. The company said it was continuing to optimise its retail footprint by reallocating resources to more efficient formats while allowing newer outlets time to mature.
The company reported net cash of Rs 69 crore in September 2026, compared with net debt of Rs 246 crore in September 2025, representing an improvement of more than Rs 300 crore.

Satyaki Ghosh, wholetime director and CEO of Raymond Lifestyle, said the company’s garmenting operations continued to benefit from changes in global supply chains, while its Branded Apparel business gained from demand for ColorPlus and Parx.

"While elevated input costs and channel mix dynamics influenced near-term operating margins, our disciplined pricing, substantial working capital contraction, and a net debt-free balance sheet with Rs 69 crore in net cash provide tremendous operational resilience," he said.

Ghosh added that domestic demand indicators remained strong ahead of the peak festive and wedding season. The company expects retail network optimisation, brand investments and capacity ramp-ups to support its stated guidance for FY27.
